#uranium #nuclear

☢️ Another supply risk for uranium—and this one involves the acid needed to extract it.

Russia’s new sulfuric-acid export restrictions appear to cover ordinary shipments to Kazakhstan, with government approval required through the end of 2026.

Russia needs Kazakh uranium, so it has a strong incentive to approve strategic deliveries. That reduces the likelihood of a severe disruption.

But it does not eliminate the risk.

Approval delays, competing demand from fertilizer producers and tight physical availability could still affect acid deliveries, mining costs and production plans.

Kazatomprom’s new TQZ acid plant is already delayed to Q3 2027–Q1 2028. It offers no immediate backup if existing supplies come under pressure.

No uranium production loss from this restriction has been confirmed. The question is how much room the supply chain has for another complication.

My bullish takeaway: nuclear growth requires dependable fuel supplies, and delivering those additional pounds remains difficult. This adds another reason for utilities to secure uranium, and for the market to put a higher value on reliable production.

It's easy to psyche yourself out of a good business idea because there’s competition.
 
“Oh someone’s already doing it, it’s too late”
 
1. Competition shows the idea might already be validated

2. Markets can be a lot bigger than you think. nobody wins a whole market anyway. Even the biggest player has like 30%. You don't need to beat them, you need a slice.

3. No one else has your unique experience and judgement. It's like thinking NYC can only support 1 pizza place. There's so many different kinds of pizza.

4. A lot of competitors are stuck in their old ways. Ex some are gonna die bc an A.I. native person's going to be way more efficient.  

I've learned to view competition as a GOOD thing. If 100 people are making money from X, I just have to be better than the guy in 100th place.

That's way easier for me mentally than entering uncharted territory and wondering if the idea's even viable.

Anyways, wanted to write this bc my friend is psych'ing himself out of an idea because he saw there's already competitors.

Batching, gasless and delegation (moreso than automation) are obvious use cases going back longer than that. It’s why we had a startup centered around it in 2020. 

A very complicated upgrade to consensus isn’t worth that though. There are simpler ways to do that. Especially for gasless and batching which are possible today. (In fact, delegation is also possible today?). The issue is lack of HW support. 

Delegation has an extra problem of verifying what rights you are granted to others (have you tried using a vault product like KPK and checking the zodiac module permissions? The UX is awful). 

Auth, I think is controversial. Not only because HW etc needs to implement it, but implementing verification algorithms for cryptographic protocols in Solidity is slow and error prone. That’s why BTCers have spent years on a super fast ecdsa / schnorr implementation.

Aka this is why I think 8130 is a mistake at consensus. It doesnt matter if a solution ticks all the boxes if it is crazy complicated and over engineered. That technical debt on nodes will be painful and probably lead to loss of user funds.
